title: Ribollita
subtitle: Tuscan bread and bean soup
excerpt: Ribollita is a thick Tuscan soup of cannellini beans, cavolo nero, and stale bread. The bread is added to the soup and stirred in until it thickens the whole pot to a dense, spoonable consistency. It is reheated the next day, which is where the name comes from: ribollita means 'reboiled'.
sourceNotes: Ribollita is a Tuscan cucina povera classic, made from the peasant practice of reboiling leftover bean and vegetable soup with stale bread to make a thick, filling meal. It is sometimes called 'la zuppa dei contadini' (the peasant soup). The dish appears in Pellegrino Artusi's La Scienza in Cucina (1891) and is most closely associated with the cooking of Florence and the surrounding Chianti hills.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the bread. Reheat, add fresh stale bread, and continue from the bread-addition step.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily. It is a large-batch soup by nature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before, cool overnight, and reheat ('ribollire') for 15 minutes the next day. The texture and flavour both improve greatly.

content.text: Ribollita is a thick Tuscan soup made from beans, vegetables, and stale bread. It is not a light vegetable soup but something denser: the bread is stirred into the pot and cooks until it absorbs the liquid and thickens the whole dish to the consistency of a very thick porridge. The name means reboiled because the soup is made one day and heated again the next. It is a winter dish, warming and substantial.

items.prepNote: stale, crusts removed, torn or sliced

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden.
Add the tinned tomatoes and rosemary. Cook for 5 minutes. Add the stock and bring to a simmer.
Mash about half the beans roughly with a fork or the back of a spoon. Add all the beans to the pot. Stir well. Add the cavolo nero and season with salt.
Simmer for 40 minutes over low heat until the cavolo nero is very soft and the soup is thick. Stir occasionally.

Add the stale bread and stir it into the soup. It will absorb the liquid and swell. Cook for a further 15 to 20 minutes until the bread has completely broken down and the soup is very thick. If it gets too stiff, add a splash of water.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve with a generous drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil and more bread alongside.

Ribollita is Tuscan peasant food from the tradition of making what little you have go as far as possible. Bean soup extended with yesterday's stale bread, reheated the next day with the remaining bread stirred in: a two-day meal from a single pot. Florence is the city most associated with the dish, though versions of it are made throughout Tuscany and into Umbria.
